title: AI World Building: two free games, a horror channel and a graphic novel
author: ShantyGameStudio
selftext:
Okay, so this is my second post with this account. I set it up for the game and had high hopes, but ADHD turned it into more of a project. I wanted to share it and plug a bit. It's a super long post, so I got Claude to do a TL;DR at the bottom as well. (Grammar isn't my thing, deal with it. That's why I have AI for the TL;DR.)

![video](kkr8d3knzn0i1)

I started with a small game after watching a video and seeing a post, similar to a lot of what I read here. I thought, I can do this, yay me. I see a lot of MMOs and RPGs, so I thought a party game that gets people playing together would be a bit more unique. So with Claude we built Sea Shanty Disaster. Dumb name, don't really care, but it was fun, and I launched it on itch and its own website. I've iterated on it a bit to make it better, but I don't really have any feedback and haven't properly posted it anywhere for people to check out. My kids had fun playing it, but it's super loud, so we don't encourage it, and they have limited screen time anyway, so all good.



Shameless plug 1: [https://shantygames.com/sea-shanty-disaster/](https://shantygames.com/sea-shanty-disaster/) (use the website, not itch. Itch's page blocks the microphone)



Then I wanted a game more to my own taste, not what my kids would like playing (they're younger girls). So I built Hush the Deep. It's an anomaly-style game. I know it's like the millionth one, but I had fun learning more with Claude, having it run Blender and Godot, and using some other tools for asset generation. I've been iterating on it too, and it's also a voice-based multiplayer game. You play as the person walking the loop finding anomalies, and you're hunted by a monster that hunts by sound. The other players are your guides. They join from their phones and see you and the monster on a sonar map. But when they talk to help you, the sound draws it in. They can also distract it by banging a pipe somewhere away from you, so you can keep searching without getting caught. I built this with limited feedback too, so I'd love to hear from the community what's working and what isn't.



Shameless plug 2: [https://shantygamestudio.itch.io/hush-the-deep](https://shantygamestudio.itch.io/hush-the-deep)   
[https://shantygames.com/hush-the-deep](https://shantygames.com/hush-the-deep) \- crew link



I used Claude for pretty well all of it, with some local image generation and Hunyuan 3D for the starting models of a couple of the 3D pieces. I'd love some feedback on the games. They're still works in progress and will stay free to play. I'll also make Hush the Deep mobile friendly when I have time.



ADHD me then decided to tie in a horror channel I have, since the game is horror, and then build a graphic novel from the channel's content. The game sort of started all of that, and it's turned into an AI-supported world that the horror game's lore lives in (we're leaving Sea Shanty Disaster out of that for now). The channel is The Small Hours on YouTube and the book is Keep Your Lights On, if anyone wants to know more.



Details from Claude below:



HUSH THE DEEP: TL;DR

A free co-op horror game. You walk one corridor on a drowned ship, spot what changed, and something blind in the ducts hunts you by sound. Your friends join from their phones (no download) as the bridge crew: sonar, intercom, the ship's manifest and a pipe to bang. I'm not a programmer: I directed and playtested, and Claude Code wrote nearly all the code in Godot 4. 2D art was made locally with Z-Image Turbo, some 3D started in Hunyuan 3D, the creature is a Blender script plus code, and the sound is licensed recordings, not AI. About 12 weeks and 244 commits, all on one PC.



What went wrong and got fixed along the way:



The monster (the biggest job by far)

\- Version 1 was a blob with tentacles that read like a cartoon octopus. A mass with arms isn't a monster, so it got a face, a mouth, and a darker, wetter, bruised look.

\- Its legs were too short to stand on, so it walked on straight rods. Its feet landed inside the crates. At the corner of the hall its body teleported and its legs got left behind. Each of those took its own fix.

\- At one point a tentacle grew straight out of its mouth.

\- It also barely showed up. The fix made it come sooner, more often, and from the end nearer you.

\- Last week it was rebuilt from scratch with no AI mesh at all: a Blender script builds the body from named anatomy (jaw, lips, ribbed throat, tentacle sockets) and exports it in about 70 seconds. It took three rounds in one day: render it from five angles, I tear it apart, rebuild. The teeth came out paper white because of a colour setting, and they now look stained and wet.

\- When it caught you up close, the game skipped straight to black. Now your head gets yanked onto its mouth first, every time.



The game

\- I had every one of the 325 places an anomaly can appear photographed in the real game lighting. 30 were too dark to ever find, and all are fixed now without lightening the hall.

\- The face in the porthole ended up hidden behind the hair on the glass. The AI looked at the screenshot and told me it was fine. It wasn't. Lesson: the AI makes things fast, but my eyes are the real quality check.

\- A name typed with a curly apostrophe broke the voice that says your name.



Multiplayer

\- An old copy of the game left running in the background could take over the public room.

\- If the connection server was down or over its daily limit, players waited forever. Now they're told.



How it stays fixed

\- Every bug gets an automated test so it can't come back. There are 33 test suites now. Without them, AI code drifts and old bugs quietly return.

\- I lost a whole session's work to a crash once, so now everything auto-commits every few messages.



SEA SHANTY DISASTER: TL;DR

What it is: a free browser party game for 2 to 6 people. You steer a raft down a kraken's throat by humming into your mic. Half the crew hums left/right and the other half hums up/down. No install, and it works on phones.



How it plays:

\- The game learns each player's vocal range, so a kid's squeak and a bass voice steer the same raft.

\- Nobody has full control, so everyone finds out who can't hold a note.

\- A recorded shanty plays behind you.

\- The raft is a cel-shaded pirate raft with a black jolly roger, and it banks as you steer.



How it was built:

\- Who did what: I set the concept, made every design call, playtested and judged. Claude Code wrote the code, build tools, tests and the art and sound pipelines. The loop was me sending back screenshots, phone recordings and one-line verdicts, and it sending builds.

\- The code: one hand-built HTML file, about 2.1 MB and about 6,400 lines. No engine or framework.

\- Multiplayer: PeerJS over WebRTC, with TURN relays for hard networks.

\- Hosting: Cloudflare Pages plus a Worker, with Supabase for telemetry.

\- Pitch detection: McLeod autocorrelation, with a median filter so held notes don't jump an octave.

\- Art: local image generation through SwarmUI (SDXL and Animagine) in an anime style. The raft is a cel-shaded Blender model rendered into a 5x5 grid of sprites, one per steering direction.

\- Quality control: separate review agents before every deploy, a custom script that catches renamed or undeclared constants, a fake-microphone harness for testing multiplayer in browser tabs, and a 16-viewport layout audit.



Timeline: the earliest files are dated 30 Jul 2026 and the latest build is 5 Nov 2026.



What went wrong (the useful part):

\- Telemetry: of the first 12 outside players, 5 got a microphone, and all 5 finished a run. The other 7 were lost at one door: itch embeds games in an iframe that blocks the mic request, and my dashboard was grouping errors by the wrong column, so every failure read "unknown" for a week.

\- Fabricated report: a local model told me it had created files it never wrote. I now check the filesystem before believing any completion report.

\- A passing syntax check isn't correctness: one renamed constant meant no private room could be joined, and every smoke test still passed.

\- Cut features: I shipped a "sing the words" mode for about a month and pulled it after playtesting.

\- The bill: my other game's relay burned the shared Cloudflare daily cap and took this one down with it.
